text: The UN and other international organisations and fora are key components of a rules-based international system.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They create a stable framework for cooperation, for managing tensions and addressing global trans-boundary problems.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The multilateral system must become more inclusive, more transparent.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Global solutions must have broad-based support from countries to be effective.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: On our part, we play our role by initiating or by catalysing the work of organisations like the Forum of Small States (FOSS) that we actually initiated, and the Global Governance Group (3G).

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we work closely with many other small states to have a greater collective voice on the international stage.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Humanitarian assistance is important and we do contribute when there are disasters and, actually, it is this training, this development that makes a longer-term impact on many other countries.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We need the support and the understanding of a united citizenry.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Ms Joan Pereira's question about how MFA can better engage the public on Singapore's foreign policy is very timely.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: While MFA takes the lead in foreign policy, issues are becoming more complex and cross-cutting in nature.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Other Ministries and Government agencies play an increasingly vital role on Singapore's external front.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: MFA must, therefore, act as a coordinator, work closely with other Ministries and agencies to pursue a whole-of-Government foreign policy and to strengthen our domestic resilience in the face of an uncertain and sometimes hostile external environment.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: This also means convincing Singaporeans of the need for consistent and principled diplomacy for our long-term interests instead of taking the path of least resistance in order to achieve short-term gains.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The events of the last six months is a reminder of this.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I am grateful for the support of Singaporeans and of Members of this House.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will continue to work with all stakeholders to raise awareness amongst our fellow Singaporeans of the stakes for us, of the principles behind our policy and of the sometimes difficult positions that we have to take, despite the pressures we will face from time to time.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Terrorism still remains a real and present threat.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Singaporeans are one of the most widely travelled people in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Senior Minister of State Dr Maliki will elaborate more on this later on.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: A united citizenry allows us to pursue effective foreign policy.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We may be small, but the unity of our people is a source of strength.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our stability, consistency and reliability are all the more valuable in an increasingly fractious world, and people respect Singapore for that.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Such respect is hard-earned, but it allows our voice to be amplified and be heard on the international stage.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I am grateful to Dr Teo Ho Pin and Mr Pritam Singh for their support for the staff of MFA and for adequate resources to be provided in the light of all these challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I totally agree with them that MFA staff must be well-staffed and well-resourced.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our MFA officers actually are the real key assets.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our budget may be the second smallest or the smallest of all the Ministries, but I think you will agree with me it is the staff of MFA.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But we also provide continuous training to nurture our staff and to develop their leadership potential.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We also regularly review our manpower resources and work functions to ensure that this precious manpower is deployed in an optimal way.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The work in MFA is very demanding and very labour-intensive and eats up all hours of the day and night.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Our officers work under very challenging conditions and at great cost to their personal and perhaps, even more so, to their family lives.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But our officers have proven themselves to be dedicated and professional.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They are driven by their mission to advance the interests of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: They understand our vulnerabilities and what we need to do in order to remain relevant.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Members of this House who have ever travelled with MFA staff, I am very sure you can attest to their professionalism and their hard work.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I want to thank Members of the House for their continued support of MFA.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: The events of the past year have been a stark reminder of the reality that Singapore faces.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But it has also provided lessons on how we can overcome these challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I think in a way, the pressure that we have come under has made us stronger and more united.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We will face another year of uncertainty ahead.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, let me start by addressing Mr Liang Eng Hwa's question on links with fellow ASEAN countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have kept up strong links with our Southeast Asian partners through high-level exchanges.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Often at the request of our friends, we shared our developmental experiences in diverse areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, Daw Aung San Suu Kyi is keen to relocate street hawkers and upgrade wet markets in Yangon.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Therefore, when Minister Vivian hosted her to breakfast, the location was at Ghim Moh Market and Food Centre so that Daw Suu could experience a typical Singapore hawker centre for herself.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Besides hosting incoming visits, our leaders make regular visits to ASEAN neighbours.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These include President Dr Tony Tan's recent State Visits to Cambodia and Laos and Minister Vivian Balakrishnan's introductory visits to Thailand, Myanmar, Laos and Vietnam.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In October last year, both President Tony Tan and Prime Minister Lee visited Thailand to pay their last respects to the late King Bhumibol Adulyadej.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Reflecting our strong people-to-people ties, many Singaporeans joined in to mourn the revered late King.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our leaders also warmly congratulated the new King Maha Vajiralongkorn when he was anointed.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Baey Yam Keng asked about strengthening our economic ties with Southeast Asian countries and how businesses can help.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We made good progress on this last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Similarly, with Laos, the launch of SilkAir's direct flights last October, along with the implementation of the Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreement this January, will create more opportunities for trade and investment.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I also made a working visit to Vietnam in July 2016 to explore opportunities for our companies to invest in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City, and to promote further liberalisation of our bilateral Air Services Agreement.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We encourage businesses to seek out opportunities for trade and investment in all our ASEAN neighbours.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Businesses should also respect the laws and local officials of their host countries and strive to be good partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If I may add, countries from outside the region are increasingly keen to partner Singapore companies for projects in Southeast Asia because of the local knowledge and the familiarity with these markets.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These partnerships are the best way to ensure that Singaporeans and Singapore companies continue to be welcomed and ties between our countries continue to grow.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will now elaborate on Minister Vivian Balakrishnan's comments on our cooperation with China and address Ms Sun Xueling's question on navigating the opportunities and challenges in our bilateral relations with China.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singapore has been a steadfast and long-standing partner and friend of China.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Several Ministers and I have just returned from Beijing where the 13th Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation (JCBC) co-chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean and Chinese Vice Premier Zhang Gaoli was just concluded.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Vice Premier Zhang and the Chinese leaders we met called Singapore an "old and good friend" of China.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The size of the delegations on both sides and the range of agencies involved show just how broad our cooperation is.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Especially in economic cooperation, the ties are also very deep.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singapore is now one of the largest offshore RMB centres outside Greater China.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: All three of our Government-to-Government projects, namely the China-Singapore Suzhou Industrial Park (SIP), the Sino-Singapore Tianjin Eco-city and the China-Singapore (Chongqing) Demonstration Initiative on Strategic Connectivity or Chongqing Connectivity Initiative, CCI in short, have supported China's developmental priorities at different stages of their growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In particular, the CCI serves as a priority demonstration project for the Belt and Road initiative by developing transport corridors linking western China and Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Apart from physical connectivity, we are discussing ways to enhance financial connectivity to support the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank's initiatives, as well as human resource development, to uplift capabilities in countries along the "Belt and Road".

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will elaborate on these areas in Mandarin.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: (In Mandarin):   Singapore has been a steadfast and long-standing partner and friend of China.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Bilateral relations started long before the establishment of diplomatic ties in 1990.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The warm and long-standing friendship between our two countries owes much to the foundation laid by Mr Lee Kuan Yew and Mr Deng Xiaoping and the continued efforts by successive generations of leaders and officials from both sides.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I was fortunate to have been involved in building our relations with China from a fairly early stage.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As a young EDB officer in the mid-1990s, I was posted to Suzhou for two years to help develop the SIP project.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But the process of working through many challenges together made our relationship more resilient.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Today, the SIP is one of China's top development zones and townships and a model for other industrial parks.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I have also made many good Chinese friends and we still keep in touch.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When I was CEO of Business China, I saw first-hand the foresight of our leaders.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With guidance from Mr Lee Kuan Yew, many Ministers contributed to efforts to groom a bilingual and bicultural group of Singaporeans who could understand and interact effectively with China.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I am glad that these exchanges with Chinese officials and cadres are continuing.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The co-chairs of the Forum on Leadership, Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean, and Central Organisation Department Minister Zhao Leji met recently in Beijing on the sidelines of the JCBC.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They agreed that the exchanges at the Forum on Leadership are valuable in addressing common challenges, such as a rapidly ageing population.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Minister Zhao also agreed to Deputy Prime Minister Teo's invitation to attend the 6th Forum on Leadership in Singapore this year to continue the exchanges.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Besides the JCBC and Forum on Leadership, the Singapore-China Social Governance Forum was launched in 2012.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The third round of this Forum was held in Singapore in May last year, co-chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Teo and Political and Legal Affairs Commission Secretary Meng Jianzhu.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We exchanged learning points on strategies to maintain security and social harmony in an increasingly urbanised society, the use of big data and IT to improve governance, as well as ensuring access to justice and the rule of law.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Other non-government organisations, such as the Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce & Industry as well as Business China, have also made important contributions to the development of bilateral relations.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Indeed, this spirit is encapsulated in the "All Round Cooperative Partnership Progressing with the Times" agreed to by Prime Minister Lee and President Xi in 2015.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singapore has been a consistent and strong supporter of China's peaceful development and engagement of the regional and international community.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We supported China's accession to the World Trade Organisation in 2001.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In 2004, we recognised China as a market economy and supported its participation in the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) and the establishment of dialogue relations with ASEAN.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are one of the earliest supporters of China's Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and Belt and Road initiative.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are very encouraged by President Xi's comments at the World Economic Forum in Davos and United Nations in Geneva that we should promote inclusive globalisation against the backdrop of a volatile and uncertain world.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The strong reservoir of friendship and goodwill allows both sides to speak candidly with one another and discuss concrete ways to elevate the relationship.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is seen in our discussion on China's Belt and Road initiative.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singapore has proposed three suggestions to our Chinese friends.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Second, greater trade, digital and financial connectivity along the Belt and Road will create investment opportunities and enhance the flow of goods and capital.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Third, Singapore and China can explore cooperation in joint training for officials from third countries along the Belt and Road.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Such development in human capital will catalyse growth and help accelerate the Belt and Road projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These ideas were welcomed by our Chinese counterparts at the JCBC and both sides have agreed to flesh out the proposals.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The title of Deputy Prime Minister Teo's recent interview with Xinhua, "New Initiatives to deepen Singapore-China Friendship(新中友谊深, 共创新思路)” captured the friendship and future cooperation between our two countries very well.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With our deep friendship and mutual trust as a strong foundation for our bilateral relations, we will forge a path forward with new areas of mutually-beneficial cooperation.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will further strengthen our special ties with China as we write the next chapter of our bilateral cooperation.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our ties with China are in good working order, resilient and well-primed for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As Vice Premier Zhang Gaoli summarised eloquently at the close of the JCBC, our bilateral relations will attain new heights.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: (In English): As Mr Zainal Sapari mentioned, besides Japan, we also have a deepening partnership with the Republic of Korea.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We share similar challenges, such as an ageing population and low birth rates.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As we embark on the Smart Nation Initiative, it is also useful for us to learn from Korea, which has a clear edge in IT and innovation in Asia.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Further afield, the Minister spoke about our partnership with the EU in response to Mr Saktiandi's question.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Indeed, Brexit is a turning point for the EU and has global consequences for trade.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Much will depend on the new relationship the UK establishes with the EU and how the UK replicates the existing agreements that the EU has with partners like Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will maintain our excellent ties with the UK, a long-standing partner in sectors, such as trade, defence, science and technology, and education.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: On the economic front, Singapore companies continue to have strong interest in the UK.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Not only is Europe a key market, we can also learn from various European countries in innovation, education and skills development, areas critical for the next phase of our economic development.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We intend to maintain the momentum of our high-level exchanges.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, the Prime Minister is scheduled to visit Germany, and the President will make State Visits to Poland and the Czech Republic later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We look forward to hosting President FranÃ§ois Hollande of France in Singapore later this month.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have been actively engaging the EU and member countries on this.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about Singapore's humanitarian assistance to other countries and whether MFA should set up a new department of Foreign Humanitarian Aid, akin to the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA).

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singapore takes our international responsibilities and commitments seriously.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As a small country with resource constraints, we want our contributions to humanitarian relief to be both sustainable and useful.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Our humanitarian assistance and disaster relief efforts are well coordinated within MFA, across relevant agencies, such as MINDEF and SCDF, and with external partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Recent examples include our contribution to the recovery efforts after the earthquake in Ecuador in April 2016, the floods and landslides in Sri Lanka in June 2016 and Hurricane Matthew in Haiti in October 2016.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We also contributed to the humanitarian and relief efforts for the victims of irregular movement of persons through the ASEAN Secretariat in September 2016.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In addition, MFA contributes annually to key international organisations that oversee and spearhead humanitarian efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These include the UN Central Emergency Response Fund and the International Committee for the Red Cross, among others.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Since 2015, we have also been partnering the UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNISDR) in providing joint training courses to strengthen the disaster risk management capacity of Small Island Developing States and other developing countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members can be assured that even with limited resources, MFA has a system in place to provide humanitarian assistance in a prompt and coordinated manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef asked about ways to improve the Singapore Cooperation Programme (SCP) and how it has helped other countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Singapore has benefited from the advice and experience of the UN and other countries, and the SCP is our way of giving back and paying it forward.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As Singapore continues to develop our capabilities, the SCP will also evolve its programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, we now offer high quality programmes in cybersecurity, digital economy and sustainable development.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To address Miss Cheng Li Hui's question, the SCP also enables us to cooperate with other countries and international agencies to address global issues, such as sustainable development and climate change.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Hence, we are partnering UN agencies and others to support the UN 2030 Sustainable Development Agenda and the Paris Agreement on Climate Change.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This year, we will collaborate with the UN Habitat to deliver an international programme in urban governance for mayors, governors and provincial leaders of African countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Besides classroom training, these new centres will rope in other Singapore agencies with development expertise, such as the Centre for Liveable Cities, Singapore International Foundation and Singapore Cooperation Enterprise, to offer technical assistance through various consultancy services and volunteer projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These will form part of our efforts to support Singapore's ASEAN Chairmanship in 2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister for Foreign Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Chairman, I will now turn the floor over to Senior Minister of State Dr Mohamad Maliki.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister Vivian Balakrishnan earlier explained the key lessons for Singapore's foreign policy as we navigate a more complex global environment today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is important for Singapore to strengthen the trust we have built with our friends across the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This trust will allow us to deepen cooperation with our partners, create opportunities for Singapore and Singaporeans abroad and advance our interests internationally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Edwin Tong have pointed out that emerging markets offer many opportunities for Singaporean businesses abroad.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Take Sub-Saharan Africa, for example, which offers opportunities for those with an appetite to venture into less familiar markets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During my visit to Ethiopia last year, I saw Ethiopia's efforts to position itself as Africa's industrial hub.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We continue to seek opportunities in other regions like South Asia, Central Asia, Russia and Turkey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For instance, we are negotiating the Sri Lanka-Singapore Free Trade Agreement, which will open doors for our businesses to expand into the vast South Asian market once concluded.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also pursuing an FTA with the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But our relationships with the emerging markets are not just economically driven.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Over the years, we have developed good political and people-to-people exchanges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, President Tony Tan made a State Visit to Mexico in June 2016 − the first State Visit by a Singapore Head of State to Latin America.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Minister Vivian will make an Official Visit to Argentina in April 2017.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have also hosted 96 Latin American journalists under the Forum for East Asia-Latin America Cooperation (FEALAC) Journalists' Visit Programme over the last 17 years, which has created greater awareness about our societies, our policies and our culture in Latin America.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For Sub-Saharan Africa, we hosted 10 ministers from the region last year to share how we tackle our urban challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It also heartens me to see more Singaporeans going off the beaten track to pursue their interests in less familiar places.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, last year, I met a lively young Singaporean lady who is studying theatre at the Waterfront Theatre School in South Africa.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: She told me that she was interested in African art and culture that led her to make such an unconventional choice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In Botswana, I was also pleasantly surprised to meet a tight-knit group of Singaporeans and learnt that several have been living there for more than a decade!

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One of the Singaporeans I met there had settled down in Botswana some 16 years ago and now operates a cow farm together with her Botswana husband.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am also glad to see our students participating in exchanges with universities in countries like Russia and Mexico.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I encourage more Singaporeans to take the road less travelled, which will broaden their perspectives while helping Singapore extend our friendships across the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore enjoys friendly relations with countries in the Middle East and it is important to continue to engage them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Understanding the complex developments in the region is important to us as 15% of our population are Muslims, many of whom visit the Middle East for the haj and umrah and for religious and Arabic language classes and studies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Today, we have about 300 students studying in Egypt and about 130 students studying in Jordan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With the Middle East presenting greater economic opportunities, more Singaporeans are working there in fields, such as hospitality, engineering, finance and transport and logistics in various countries, such as Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Oman.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In 2015, our Consulate-General in Dubai was designated as an overseas polling station for elections to make it easier for Singaporeans in the region to cast their votes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This is in recognition of the growing number of Singaporeans in that region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We also cooperate closely with some Middle Eastern countries in areas, such as education, environment and security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We recognise that the security situation in the Middle East will have implications for our region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: That is why Singapore has contributed to the international coalition against the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria (ISIS), while our Navy participates in anti-piracy operations in the Gulf of Aden.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There remains keen interest in the Middle East countries to learn from Singapore's development experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Over the past three years, there were more than 100 study visits in areas such as urban planning, port management and education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Low oil prices have also forced the oil-dependent Middle East countries to implement economic reforms and diversify their economies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There continues to be opportunities in sectors where Singapore companies have expertise in, such as transport and logistics, healthcare, water technology and education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As a small state, we maintain friendly ties with all who want to befriend us, including those from the Middle East.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Prime Minister Lee visited Jordan, Israel and the Palestinian Territories last year in April.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During the trip, Prime Minister Lee invited the leaders of Jordan, the Palestinian National Authority (PNA) and Israel to visit Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's reciprocal visit took place just last week.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore and Israel have a longstanding relationship, dating back to when the Israelis helped us build up our SAF and thereby secure our independence and sovereignty.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We look forward to welcoming the leaders from Jordan and the PNA to Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin asked about Singapore's position on the Israeli-Palestinian issue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have good relations with both Israel and PNA, and many Arab countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During his visit to Israel last year and during Prime Minister Netanyahu's recent visit to Singapore, Prime Minister Lee had clearly articulated Singapore's long-standing and consistent position on the Middle East Peace Process, including our support for the two-state solution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While Singapore supports Israel's right to live within secure borders and in peace, at the same time, we also support the right of the Palestinian people to a homeland.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have consistently voted in favour of most of the Palestinian-related resolutions tabled at the UN General Assembly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore also enjoys friendly relations with the Palestinians.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Over the years, Singapore leaders have made visits to Ramallah and we do our best to help the Palestinians rebuild their lives as well as develop their economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To follow up on the Prime Minister's visit, I visited Ramallah, as well as Israel and Jordan, in November last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During the visit, I informed the PNA leaders about the Government's appointment of Mr Hawazi Daipi as Singapore's Representative to the PNA to help coordinate our assistance to the PNA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Hawazi has since made his first visit to the West Bank as Representative in January this year where he met a number of senior office holders and officials from the PNA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One of the officials, PNA Assistant Foreign Minister Mazen Shamia, expressed the Palestinian leadership's "happiness and satisfaction" with the "remarkable development" of ties between the Palestinians and Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During my visit to Ramallah, I had the opportunity to meet senior Palestinian alumni of our Singapore Cooperation Programme (SCP).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We welcome the Palestinians' interest in our SCP courses and are working closely with the PNA to identify the critical areas where Singapore can contribute to capacity-building in the Palestinian Territories, within our limited resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One of the areas where we may be able to assist the Palestinians is in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With over a third of the Palestinian population under age 30, equipping these youths with skills relevant to the marketplace is critical to the economic development and viability of the Palestinian Territories.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In this regard, we invited PNA Minister of Education and Higher Education Sabri Saidam to visit Singapore from 31 October to 2 November 2016 to learn more about Singapore's approach to TVET, while ITE Education Services visited the West Bank in January 2017 to conduct a TVET skills needs analysis for the Palestinians.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Following the Prime Minister's visit, we have received many requests for study visits and training courses in non-TVET fields, too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This year, we hope to welcome Palestinian officials to Singapore to study our industrial estate management policies, among others.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Hawazi is also planning to visit the Palestinian Territories later this year to explore further areas of cooperation between Singapore and the PNA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin also asked about the impact of international conferences, such as the Conference for Peace in the Middle East, held in January this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Conference was held in Paris on 15 January 2017 and involved leaders and senior officials from some 70 countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Although Singapore was not a member of the Conference, we are supportive of all efforts by the international community to facilitate the resumption of meaningful and direct negotiations towards a two-state solution, whereby Israel and Palestine can live side-by-side in peace and security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, as I have said earlier, developments in the Middle East have security implications for us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have observed how ISIS has exported its ideology through the Internet and other social media platforms, radicalising individuals in the US, Europe and even here in Southeast Asia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef asked how we are preparing to manage such a challenging security climate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: ISIS has suffered several military setbacks recently in Iraq and Syria.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While we have our counter-terrorism strategy, Singapore cannot tackle this trans-border threat alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MFA will continue to keep up regular political exchanges and community engagement across our region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During my trip to Dhaka, Bangladesh, in October 2016, I shared Singapore's experiences with the local Muslim community over there and heard about their efforts to instil the correct message about Islam.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must continue working closely with foreign counterparts to share intelligence, coordinate approaches and encourage the exchange of best practices on how to counter radical ideologies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In light of the spate of terror attacks across the globe, Ms Joan Pereira has asked how MFA is better preparing itself to help Singaporeans caught in crisis situations abroad.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In 2016 alone, major consular incidents included the terror attacks in Brussels and Nice, the bombings and unrest in Turkey, earthquakes in the region and the Muar Bus Accident.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With Singaporeans being one of the most well-travelled people in the world, this raises not only the volume but also the complexity of consular cases that MFA has to handle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With finite resources, we have to work hard and be creative to respond to consular incidents quickly and effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Alongside a limited number of overseas missions, MFA officers are rostered 24/7 so that Singaporeans can contact MFA and vice versa during emergency situations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During the tragic bus accident that took place on the North-South Highway in Muar on Christmas Eve last year, MFA sent an officer quickly to reinforce the Singapore Consulate in Johor Bahru.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also enhancing our MFA@SG app to include a safety check feature to allow e-registrants to update MFA on their safety status using their mobile devices during crisis situations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are expanding our IT platforms to allow e-Registration and safety checks using chat-bots.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It will soon be easier to find information on our websites through a Virtual Assistant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We urge Singaporeans to do their part and take the necessary precautions by staying vigilant, purchasing travel insurance, and staying in touch with family and friends so that they know you are safe during your travels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: E-registrants will receive information on how to contact our nearest overseas mission and MFA can quickly contact e-registered Singaporean travellers during emergencies to ascertain the need for urgent assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: So, I cannot emphasise again how important it is for Singaporeans to e-register.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For instance, one citizen who was in the locality of a man-made disaster in China complained that other Singaporeans were contacted by MFA to ascertain their safety, but wondered why MFA had missed contacting him.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: But when we investigated, we realised that he had not e-registered so there was no way MFA could know that he was in the area at that time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: If more of these Singaporeans had e-registered, it would allow us to more quickly verify if they have been confirmed safe or if they require urgent assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In many emergency situations, e-registration has allowed us to contact affected Singaporeans, and one incident last year comes to mind.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During the attempted coup in Turkey in July 2016, MFA contacted all registered Singaporeans in the affected areas and monitored the situation closely.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In the same month, 86 people were killed after a terrorist drove a cargo truck into crowds celebrating Bastille Day in Nice, France.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Similarly, MFA contacted all registered Singaporeans in France to verify their safety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: After ascertaining that a Singaporean student was seriously injured during that attack, our Embassy staff was on the ground to extend consular assistance to the Singaporean and his parents who had flown to Nice to be with him.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: On that note, I would like to thank Ms Joan Pereira for commending our MFA officers for their dedication in discharging their consular duties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The nature of consular work is challenging and complex.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our officers often work hard around the clock to provide support to distressed Singaporeans abroad.

speaker: The Chairman
text: If there are no clarifications, Mr Vikram Nair, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang
text: What will be the Minister's approach, facing such a counterpart?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think this tension between a rules-based world order and a power-based world order will always be there.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: When I meet my counterparts, I explain to them that because we are a tiny city state and we live in a tough neighbourhood, Singapore has no choice but to subscribe to international laws.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, as a matter of principle, we stand for it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I will also tell Members, quite frankly, that big superpowers sometimes − and it is not only one; all of them, if you look through international jurisprudence − have, from time to time, taken liberties with international law.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have to quietly, non-provocatively just stand up to state our position.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But we are in no position to enforce it.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That is actually very difficult, and it is impossible to enforce international law, except through moral suasion and through mutual agreement between countries.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We just had the ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Retreat two weeks ago.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We should be able to get through this year successfully.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I give my full assurance of support to the Philippines.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: In fact, they both relate to relations with the US and China.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: First, I think Singapore has always found a way to look for opportunities in the midst of adversity or difficult situations.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: So, what opportunities does MFA see with the new US administration?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I know that it is still starting; it is finding its feet.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: But what are the possible opportunities we can have to build bridges and do things together with the US?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: It seems to be that China itself may be open to persuasion that international norms and rules are important, vital, and will be the way forward.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Is there any opportunity that we can persuade more people that rules-based international order is in everyone's best interest?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As I have explained just now, I think the outlook of US policies and programmes is still evolving.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The most recent speech by President Trump to the Joint Session of Congress was a far more positive and far more, I would say, conciliatory speech.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We look forward to those sentiments being translated into policy and actions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If you also parse his comments carefully, he says he is pro-business.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: He also says he believes in free trade, but he wants it to be fair trade.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think this is actually not an unreasonable position.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, it is the duty of every national trade negotiator – you engage in either bilateral or regional negotiations to make sure that the terms of the agreement are fair and actually improve the overall position of your own country.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The point is it is the duty of your own negotiator to secure the best terms possible.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: An important point about trade – and this is the political point – is that the advantages of free trade are sometimes not totally symmetrical with all segments of your population.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Therefore, free trade has to be accompanied by domestic policy, which makes sure you address the needs of specific segments, especially the more vulnerable segments of your population.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That is why you see – and this is a larger point that goes beyond foreign policy − in case of Singapore, we say we have no choice but to operate the free trade system.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But we also actually are very socialist when it comes to housing, education and healthcare.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: You see so much of the Budget policy actually being focused on vulnerable groups: people or segments of our population who would otherwise be vulnerable to the vagaries of free trade.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There is a complex interplay between domestic policy and foreign policy.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: If you can get your domestic policy right, it makes foreign policy and international trade so much easier.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I do not want to be cynical about the evolution of US policy.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: At the same time, I do not want to trivialise and assume everything will be hunky dory.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But every time we engage the US, we remind them that the last 70 years since the end of the Second World War has been, in a sense, a golden age for the world.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Despite the Cold War, no nuclear weapons were fired in anger.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Yes, there were proxy battles in the earlier part of the Cold War.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But, actually, what you have seen, let us say, since 1978 in China, and 1991 in India, there has been an incredible upliftment of hundreds of millions of people from abject poverty.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Through the free market, through bringing down barriers, through investing in infrastructure, through economic integration.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This has allowed a win-win proposition to be played out across the entire world and allowed people to achieve peace, stability and prosperity, without war and without engaging in zero-sum rivalry.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The larger philosophical point we have to keep advancing on the international stage is to look for win-win outcomes and not to be trapped in prisoners' dilemmas or in zero-sum games.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We advance this by being an honest broker, by being consistent in what we say and what we do, and by offering ourselves.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: People cannot copy our solutions but we say, "Look at the way Singapore and the way ASEAN have progressed in the last 50 years.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But, substantially, the direction of interdependence, mutual cooperation, win-win outcomes is the correct strategic direction." Did the Member have a second clarification?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The hon Member Mr Vikram Nair stood at his seat to repeat his second clarification.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think if we can get a critical mass to operate on a rules-based system, to operate free trade, accompanied by appropriate domestic safeguards and social security nets and then you prove it by succeeding.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Again, this is not a debate; it is not a form of words that will settle it.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Chairman, just a quick question for the Minister, and it follows from the point I made in the cut about the Committee on the Future Economy (CFE) and the prospect of more consulates, more assistance for our businesses.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I heard Senior Minister of State Josephine Teo speak about China and the number of consulates which we have in that country.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: For that, we take people from outside the Civil Service, in the business sector and others, who know the countries and are able to carry the flag of Singapore high and open opportunities for other Singaporeans in an altruistic way.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We are also blessed to have that additional element.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We have incredible career officers, while we are also supplemented by a cadre of well-meaning, high-achieving Singaporeans.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Vikram Nair, if you do not have any more clarifications, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: As I had said, they took us on a tour of the world but I think that really tells you how much hard work MFA has been doing.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: And I personally must record my thanks to the MFA staff every time I have been on a trip with them.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my cut.
